field.label: Enabled
field.help: Keep a DHCP lease alive for the selected CARP virtual IP.

field.label: CARP virtual IP
field.help: The CARP virtual IP to keep a lease for. Interface, VHID and IP are derived from it; the DHCP client MAC (chaddr) is the CARP virtual MAC for that VHID, so the lease follows the VIP to the peer on failover.

field.label: IPv4 lease policy
field.help: What the keeper does with the address the DHCP server gives. Follow dynamic address (the default): a different address than the configured VIP is accepted and the CARP virtual IP is rewritten to match, so the VIP stays online on a dynamic line. Both HA nodes converge on the same address because they share the chaddr (the server gives one lease per chaddr). Pair it with "Sync firewall alias" so outbound NAT and rules follow the new address. Enforce reservation: for a fixed reservation; a different address raises a mismatch alarm instead of being accepted. Enforce reservation and fail over on loss: as Enforce, and this node also demotes itself, handing the CARP virtual IP to the peer, when it stops holding the lease.

field.label: Sync firewall alias
field.help: Optional. The plugin creates and maintains a firewall Host alias with this name, always set to this CARP VIP's current address. Point your outbound NAT translation address (and any firewall rules that must follow the address) at this alias, so they follow automatically when "Follow dynamic address" changes it (applied by a state-preserving filter reload). NOTE: inbound port-forwards cannot follow a dynamic address (the upstream only routes inbound to a reserved address). The plugin never deletes the alias. See the plugin README.

field.label: DHCP hostname
field.help: Optional DHCP option 12 (hostname). Empty = not sent. Unlike the WAN interface's Hostname field, this does not also set the client identifier: if that field was set before you moved to the keeper (Interfaces > WAN, DHCP client section), put the same text here, and in advanced mode set Client identifier to From Send Options with the line dhcp-client-identifier "the same text" in Send Options.

field.label: Client MAC override (chaddr)
field.help: Leave blank. By default the keeper's DHCP client uses the CARP virtual MAC, which is what you want: the lease, the ISP's IP-to-MAC binding and the VIP's own outbound traffic all sit on one MAC, and the lease follows the VIP to the peer on failover. Override ONLY if your ISP has a fixed reservation bound to a specific, different MAC that you cannot change. Do NOT enter this node's own interface MAC: the VIP still sends from the CARP virtual MAC, so on an ISP that binds the leased IP to the MAC (IP source guard) the gateway becomes unreachable ("No route to host"). Empty = the derived CARP virtual MAC. A Client identifier of Default follows this MAC.

field.label: Client identifier
field.help: DHCP option 61, the client identity some ISPs use instead of the MAC address. Default: hardware type 1 + the client MAC (the CARP virtual MAC, or the override above), the same as a normal OPNsense WAN with an empty Hostname field. Both HA nodes send the same identity by design. None: no option 61 is sent; keepers upgraded from a version that sent none keep this. From Send Options: the dhcp-client-identifier line in Send Options (text in quotes, or colon-separated hex). Changing this changes the identity the ISP sees, so an ISP that uses option 61 may refuse the keeper until the old lease runs out, or give a new address. Only if normal WAN DHCP still runs on the same interface next to the keeper, the two must have different identities.

field.label: Use VLAN priority
field.help: Certain ISPs require DHCP requests sent with a specific VLAN priority (802.1p), like this field on the interface page. The keeper sets it on everything it sends: DHCP, including renewals and release, and ARP nudges. Best Effort (0) works like Disabled here: frames keep the priority of the VLAN device. On an interface that is not a VLAN, frames get a priority tag with VLAN ID 0. Needs the tunable net.link.vlan.mtag_pcp at 1 (the default); the status page warns if it is 0.

field.label: Send Options
field.help: Extra DHCP options some ISPs require, one per line as on the interface page: name value. Text in double quotes, or colon-separated hex for the options that take it (option-N and a few named ones). Example: user-class "+FSVDSL_livebox.Internet.softathome.Livebox5" or option-90 00:00:00:00. Sent in every request and renewal; a release carries only the client identifier (option 61), also when it comes from here. The vendor class (option 60) goes here as dhcp-class-identifier "..."; the client identifier (option 61) as dhcp-client-identifier ... when Client identifier is From Send Options; the hostname (option 12) is the Hostname field. Values are never shown outside this dialog.

field.label: Request Options
field.help: DHCP options to ask the server for, one name per line, as on the interface page. They are added in this order before the options the keeper always asks for (subnet mask, router, lease and renewal times, server identifier), never replacing them. This only shapes the request: the keeper does not apply DNS servers, routes or other values from the reply.

field.label: Own default route by CARP role
field.help: Default OFF. Make this keeper own the IPv4 default route (0.0.0.0/0) by CARP role: the master node holding this keeper's lease keeps a default via the lease gateway, every other state keeps none, so a node offers a default only while it can actually route one (a failover moves it, a backup withdraws it, instead of black-holing). Off: inert. Observe: log the decision it would make, without touching the routing table (use this first). Enforce: actually install and withdraw the default. Only ONE keeper (the WAN VIP) may enforce. In enforce mode, also tick the WAN gateway's "Mark Gateway as Down" (force_down) so OPNsense does not install a competing default. With os-frr the redistributed kernel default then follows the CARP role automatically; it also works without FRR. To give the backup internet while it holds no default, see Backup egress (advanced mode). See the README.

field.label: Backup egress (internet while not master)
field.help: Default OFF. While this node is the CARP backup (and so holds no WAN default), route its OWN internet traffic (updates, NTP, DNS) to the master, which NATs it out the single WAN. Needs "Own default route by CARP role" set to observe or enforce; the route is removed automatically when this node becomes master. See the backup-egress docs.

field.label: Backup egress route form
field.help: /1-split (recommended): 0.0.0.0/1 + 128.0.0.0/1, full internet but not the default, so it never redistributes as a default nor collides with enforce. Specific prefixes: only the CIDR destinations listed below.

field.label: Backup egress gateway
field.help: The next hop = "the master". Best a stable internal CARP VIP (e.g. the LAN VIP), which always points at the master and follows failover; or a separate fallback-WAN gateway (independent egress). Leave blank to derive the peer automatically from the point-to-point /30 or /31 interface set below. Do not enter a plain peer address that differs per node: it syncs identically and would be wrong on one node.

field.label: Backup egress interface (for auto-derive)
field.help: Only used when the gateway above is blank: a point-to-point /30 or /31 interface (typically the SYNC link) whose other host is the master. The peer is derived per node, so it stays correct after a failover. Enter the interface device name.

field.label: Backup egress prefixes
field.help: Only used with route form "Specific prefixes": the IPv4 CIDR destinations to route via the gateway, added one per token (CIDR notation like 10.0.0.0/24). Do not list 0.0.0.0/0.

field.label: ARP nudge interval (s)
field.help: Periodically broadcast an ARP request from the VIP (with its CARP virtual MAC) for the upstream gateway, so the gateway's ARP entry for the VIP never expires. Use when the upstream ignores gratuitous ARP and never re-ARPs an expired entry. The symptom is that traffic NATed to the VIP works right after a CARP event or DHCP exchange, then silently blackholes some minutes later (outbound packets leave, nothing returns). Only sent while this node is CARP master for the VIP. Default: 120 (on), one broadcast ARP per interval; lower toward the 30 s floor if a short-ARP-timeout gateway still blackholes the VIP between nudges. Setting 0 disables the nudge entirely: the periodic nudge, the automatic nudge on CARP failover AND the manual nudge button on the status page (the early lease renew on failover is unaffected).

field.label: ARP listen in promiscuous mode
field.help: Fallback, default OFF. Applies only while the ARP nudge is enabled (interval > 0), since it only helps capture the nudge's reply; it is ignored when the nudge is off. The keeper listens for the gateway's ARP reply to each nudge and shows on the Status page when the gateway last confirmed reachability. Normally the reply is captured without promiscuous mode (the CARP master already accepts the VIP's MAC). Enable this ONLY if the Status page shows the nudge is never confirmed on a bound master, since some NICs drop frames addressed to a non-primary unicast MAC unless the interface is promiscuous. WARNING: promiscuous mode makes this root daemon receive ALL traffic on the segment, not just its own; leave it off unless you need it.
